signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Holds ~$57.5 as a haven through the FOMC selloff; caught between a hawkish Fed and the reignited war premium
signals.detail: Silver spot ~$57.5 (~flat, Wed 29 Jul); gold ~$4,029; GDX ~$74.2 (Tue close)
signals.takeaway: The book's single most important line item was resilient on FOMC day: silver held roughly flat at ~$57.5 while US equities sold off hard on the hawkish hold, as the reignited US-Iran conflict (oil +8%) and haven demand offset a firmer dollar. Silver is now caught in a two-sided pull — a hawkish Fed and higher 10Y (~4.64%) are the bearish real-rate channel, while the war/inflation premium is the bullish one. Structural deficit thesis holds (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit; JPMorgan ~$81 avg). Hold the core and hedge the silver-vs-gold spread into Thu's PCE print rather than adding leverage.

signals.name: Crude oil / Energy
signals.label: US-Iran pause BREAKS: oil spikes ~+8% (Brent ~$90.7, WTI ~$84.5) on renewed strikes and Red Sea attacks
signals.detail: Brent +7.9% to ~$90.74, WTI +6.6% to ~$84.46 (Wed 29 Jul); pause collapsed on renewed airstrikes, Houthi Red Sea embargo, Trump warning
signals.takeaway: The dominant cross-portfolio driver flipped: the US-Iran fighting pause that had held since ~27 Jul collapsed on Wednesday — renewed airstrikes, a Trump warning that Iran 'is going to get a beating', repeated Hormuz tanker attacks and a Houthi maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia — sending Brent up ~8%. Energy was the only green sector as everything else fell. Double-edged for the book: it re-arms the inflation/rate-hike fear that pressures the rate-sensitive core (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech, crypto) right as the Fed turned hawkish, but restores the geopolitical bid under gold/silver and lifts the small energy long. Trade the pause-breaks-vs-re-holds odds; the Red Sea/Hormuz front is the live escalation risk.

signals.name: US Treasuries / rates
signals.label: Fed hawkish hold 9-3: three hike dissents, 10Y jumps to ~4.64%; September now a live hike risk
signals.detail: Held 3.50-3.75%; 9-3 vote (Hammack/Kashkari/Logan dissent for a hike); 10Y ~4.64% (+~7bp), 2Y ~4.3%, DXY ~101.4; core PCE Thu
signals.takeaway: The Fed held for a fifth straight meeting but the decision read hawkish — three regional-president dissents wanting a hike, a terse Warsh statement, 'won't hesitate' on inflation and no September guidance — and the bond market judged the Fed behind, sending the 10Y up ~7bp to ~4.64% and the dollar firmer. That is the direct higher-for-longer headwind for the book's highest-beta pain (levered silver, gold miners) and for S-REITs, and September is now a live hike risk. The big USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as productive dry powder for the shakeout. Thu's Q2 GDP and core PCE are the immediate binary — a hot print validates the dissents and lifts September odds; a cool one caps the yield backup.

signals.name: Gold / gold miners
signals.label: Holds ~$4,029 above $4,000 through the selloff; drew the largest weekly fund inflow since April
signals.detail: Gold ~$4,029 (~flat, Wed 29 Jul), above the $4,000 line; gold funds +$2.0bn (wk to 22 Jul, largest since April); GDX ~$74.2
signals.takeaway: Gold was resilient on FOMC day — holding ~$4,029 above $4,000 and gaining modestly after the hold as the reignited Middle East conflict and the equity selloff drew a haven bid that offset the firmer dollar. It held far better than the beta names and drew the largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April (+$2.0bn), with multi-month central-bank buying a structural floor. Favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage as the steadier metals hold and the cleaner hedge against the Iran pause staying broken; BofA's flagged elevated net-longs are the near-term warning. The ~$4,130 two-week high is the level to reclaim.

signals.name: Semiconductors / AI-capex
signals.label: Chip rout extends: SMH -4%, >$1trn wiped since 24 Jul, Nasdaq 100 in correction; MSFT vs META split the AI-capex verdict
signals.detail: SMH -4% Wed (~-9% 1-mo); >$1trn erased since 24 Jul; Nasdaq 100 ~-10% from June peak; MSFT +3% AH (Azure +43%), META -7% AH on $125-145B capex guide
signals.takeaway: The AI-chip selloff deepened into a valuation-regime shift, not a one-day scare — SMH -4% Wednesday, more than $1trn wiped from global semi/AI-hardware caps since 24 Jul, and the Nasdaq 100 into a ~10% correction on AI-overcapacity fears (Meta's 'Meta Compute' surplus plan). The post-close earnings split the debate: MSFT beat and rose +3% AH on capex discipline (Azure +43%), while META beat but fell -7% AH on its elevated $125-145B FY26 capex guide. A direct, deepening headwind for the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core — favor the internet/platform names (Tencent, Xiaomi) over pure semis; AAPL/AMZN (Thu) are the next read.

signals.name: Rare earths (ex-China basket)
signals.label: Lynas makes first ex-China terbium; MP/USAR on China entity list; 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff nears
signals.detail: Lynas first commercial-scale terbium oxide outside China + reported ~US$96M DoD deal; MP & USAR on China dual-use entity list (22 Jun); broad MOFCOM controls SUSPENDED to 10 Nov 2026
signals.takeaway: The China/US rare-earth decoupling structurally favors the ex-China watchlist: Lynas produced the first commercial-scale terbium separation outside China (a heavy-REE milestone) and advanced its ~US$96M US DoD supply deal, while MP carries DoD backing (~15% stake, $110/kg NdPr floor) and Energy Fuels builds out White Mesa. But MP and USA Rare Earth sit on China's entity-specific dual-use control list (added 22 Jun) and the broad October-2025 MOFCOM controls are suspended only until 10 Nov 2026 (~3.5 months out) — the calendar catalyst. This stays a strategic optionality play on the controls snapping back, not an immediate momentum trade: accumulate MP and government-backed UUUU on weakness into that 10 Nov cliff.

signals.name: Tencent / HK tech
signals.label: Tencent suspends buyback into a 12 Aug-results blackout; internet sleeve still favored over the SMIC chip leg
signals.detail: Tencent buybacks (1.1M sh/HK$500.7M on 9 Jul) SUSPENDED from ~22 Jul into a 30-day blackout ahead of 12 Aug results; record China inflow (+$21.3bn) the prior week; Xiaomi buyback 3.9M sh/HK$100.7M (15 Jul)
signals.takeaway: The HK-tech core's internet names had been decoupling from the global chip rout and drew a record China weekly inflow (+$21.3bn) under the 24 Jul Politburo H2-stimulus signal — but Tencent has now suspended its near-daily buyback from ~22 Jul, entering the customary blackout ahead of its 12 Aug interim results, temporarily removing a mechanical corporate bid into a jittery, post-FOMC tape. Xiaomi's own buyback continues. Favor Tencent/Xiaomi (internet/consumer) over the SMIC chip leg while the AI-capex unwind runs, but don't add aggressively before the 12 Aug print; US risk-off and a hawkish Fed are the near-term beta headwinds, and the pre-selloff China inflow needs the 31 Jul Flow Show to confirm it held.

Sits opposite the Micron/AI bulls (Newhouse) and validates Burry's standing chip shorts — the congressional book splitting on the AI-capex debate. A direct read-through to the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core.

The META/MSFT legs land right into their post-close prints (MSFT +3% AH, META -7% AH). Lands the same day as Liccardo's NVDA sell, capturing the two-sided AI-capex debate within Congress.

A rare direct overlap with the portfolio's PM-miner sleeve, and well-timed as oil re-spiked ~8% on the Iran-pause breakdown.

The Intel leg lands as INTC restructures under state/government-backstop chatter; the Uber leg extends the household's mega-cap tech/mobility tilt. superInvestors.name: Scion / Michael Burry (personal)
superInvestors.rationale: Having deregistered Scion with the SEC in Nov 2025 (now liquidating), Burry trades personally and discloses only via a voluntary newsletter — a May 2026 post claimed ~80% of the book in NVDA/PLTR puts (~$1.1B notional), and he has since described expanding chip shorts (NVDA, MU, AMAT, SOXX, TSLA, CAT), arguing hyperscalers are stretching GPU depreciation toward a write-down/order-cut cycle — 'the beginning of the end' of the chip boom.
superInvestors.deepDive: These are his freshest, most public bets and they kept working into the late-July rout — the semis complex shed >$1trn since 24 Jul (SMH -4% Wed) as AI-overcapacity fears (Meta's surplus-capacity plan) drove a valuation-regime shift. The cleanest smart-money expression of the AI-capex-peak thesis, directly opposite the Micron/AI buys in some congressional books (Newhouse) and the crowded AI-infra longs (Ackman/Tepper/Bridgewater). No 13F any longer — the newsletter is the only window; self-reported, sizes approximate, not SEC filings.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.value: AAPL+GOOGL now ~30% of the equity book

A striking contrast with Duquesne's Q1 GOOGL exit. Q2 13F due 14 Aug — confirm the sell-streak and any new adds then.

The four teased positions plus the Pershing Square USA IPO prep make his 14 Aug 13F one of the most-watched of the cycle. No fresh activist 13D surfaced this run.

superInvestors.rationale: George Soros's fund held an S&P 500 put as its top position ($773M) and added NVDA, TSM and EA while cutting Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft in Q1 — a hedged, cautious posture. No new 13D/13G surfaced mid-cycle.
superInvestors.deepDive: The large index-put top holding is a portfolio hedge that looks prescient into the 28-29 Jul FOMC selloff — capturing the defensive tilt among some whales into a stretched tape. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.rationale: The Gates Foundation Trust held a concentrated ~$31.7B book (top: Berkshire, Waste Management, Canadian National, Caterpillar, Deere) with no notable individual change and no July 13D/13G filing — a low-turnover, blue-chip reference book.
superInvestors.deepDive: Included as a stable long-horizon 'permanent capital' benchmark; its concentration and inactivity contrast with the high-turnover hedge funds. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.name: Trump / Trump Media (DJT)
superInvestors.rationale: Forbes pegs Trump's net worth at ~$6.1B, dominated by the ~41% DJT stake and ~$1.4B of crypto-linked lines. A 19 Jul SEC corporate update detailed Trump Media's crypto-treasury build — ~9,542 BTC (~$593M) plus a ~$2B additional BTC purchase (~$2.6B total) — while recent DJT Form 4s are RSU grants, NOT open-market buys.

The absence of any insider open-market purchase and the RSU-heavy Form 4 activity are the recent corporate developments.

superInvestors.deepDive: Included for roster completeness; no material change verified this run (gap).
